statement:
Let $S$ be locally Noetherian and universally catenary with dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, use $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for an integral closed subscheme $W\subset T$ write $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

The abelian group $Z_q(T)$ consists of locally finite integral linear combinations of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$. For a closed subscheme $A$ of dimension at most $q$, let $[A]_q$ sum the $q$-dimensional components with multiplicities $\operatorname{length}_{\mathcal O_{T,\eta}}\mathcal O_{A,\eta}$. Let $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ be $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite sums of principal Weil divisors on integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q+1$.

For an invertible sheaf $\mathcal M$ on an integral scheme $W$ and a nonzero meromorphic section $u$, define $\operatorname{div}_{\mathcal M}(u)$ as the Weil divisor whose coefficients at codimension-one integral closed subschemes are orders of the local meromorphic function representing $u$ in a trivialization; at a height-one local domain $A$, for $a,b\in A\setminus\{0\}$, the order of $a/b$ is $\operatorname{length}_A(A/aA)-\operatorname{length}_A(A/bA)$. The class of this divisor in $\mathrm{CH}_{\dim_\delta(W)-1}(W)$ is $c_1(\mathcal M)\cap[W]$. For a global section $u$, $Z(u)$ is its scheme-theoretic zero locus.

For a flat morphism $h:T'\to T$ of relative dimension $r$, the pullback $h^*:Z_q(T)\to Z_{q+r}(T')$ sends $[W]$ to the cycle $[T'\times_T W]_{q+r}$ with scheme-theoretic multiplicities. It also induces a map on Chow groups.

Let $X$, $Y$ be locally of finite type over $S$.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a flat morphism of relative dimension $r$.
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible sheaf on $Y$.
Assume $Y$ is integral and $n = \dim_\delta(Y)$.
Let $s$ be a nonzero meromorphic section of $\mathcal{L}$.
Then we have
$$
f^*\text{div}_\mathcal{L}(s) = \sum n_i\text{div}_{f^*\mathcal{L}|_{X_i}}(s_i)
$$
in $Z_{n + r - 1}(X)$. Here the sum is over the irreducible
components $X_i \subset X$ of $\delta$-dimension $n + r$,
the section $s_i = f|_{X_i}^*(s)$ is the pullback of $s$, and
$n_i = m_{X_i, X}$ is the multiplicity of $X_i$ in $X$.

Let $X$, $Y$ be locally of finite type over $S$.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a flat morphism of relative dimension $r$.
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible sheaf on $Y$.
Let $\alpha$ be a $k$-cycle on $Y$.
Then
$$
f^*(c_1(\mathcal{L}) \cap \alpha) = c_1(f^*\mathcal{L}) \cap f^*\alpha
$$
in $\mathrm{CH}_{k + r - 1}(X)$.

Let $X$, $Y$ be locally of finite type over $S$.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a proper morphism.
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible sheaf on $Y$.
Let $s$ be a nonzero meromorphic section $s$ of $\mathcal{L}$ on $Y$.
Assume $X$, $Y$ integral, $f$ dominant, and $\dim_\delta(X) = \dim_\delta(Y)$.
Then
$$
f_*\left(\text{div}_{f^*\mathcal{L}}(f^*s)\right) =
[R(X) : R(Y)]\text{div}_\mathcal{L}(s).
$$
as cycles on $Y$. In particular
$$
f_*(c_1(f^*\mathcal{L}) \cap [X]) =
[R(X) : R(Y)] c_1(\mathcal{L}) \cap [Y] =
c_1(\mathcal{L}) \cap f_*[X]
$$
